code_actions.rationale: Imaging and provider documentation (admission H&P and radiology) confirm a left basal-ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage with IVH and obstructive hydrocephalus, meeting the policy's ICH validation criteria.
No radiology or consult documentation supports a subdural hemorrhage; imaging and consults document a basal-ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage with IVH instead.
Imaging and neurosurgery documentation describe obstructive hydrocephalus due to IVH with emergent CSF diversion; policy designates obstructive hydrocephalus as MCC when criteria are met.
The chart documents cerebral salt wasting (treated with fludrocortisone) rather than SIADH; there is no documentation supporting SIADH, so E22.2 is unsupported.
Dense right hemiplegia is documented on initial exam and progress notes; POA should be Y. Billed laterality is supported; change POA to reflect presence on arrival.
Admission H&P documents inability to speak on presentation; dysarthria/aphasia is present on admission.
The record documents a VP shunt and EVD but no intracranial neurostimulator operative note or device documentation; absence of any neurostimulator documentation makes Z98.62 unsupported.
Emergent intubation at presentation and later tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status at transfer are documented; dependence on ventilator/trach should be coded as present on admission/encounter.
No documentation of meningococcal meningitis was found; the infectious complication documented was Klebsiella VAP. A39.0 is unsupported.

No procedural note or operative report documenting insertion of an infusion device into the SVC was found in the retrieved chart; discharge and procedure summaries list other devices (EVD, VP shunt, tracheostomy, PEG, arterial line) but not an infusion device into the SVC.

policy_citations.quote: [1] Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is not documented. Emergent intubation may preclude room-air measurement; provider documentation of the clinical urgency is sufficient.

system_note: Claim MR_19 billed a principal diagnosis of I61.9 (Nontraumatic ICH) plus multiple high-severity comorbidities and invasive procedures. Review of the record against the governing condition policies shows the core cerebrovascular/critical-care coding is supported (intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH, obstructive hydrocephalus, EVD and subsequent VP shunt, prolonged mechanical ventilation with tracheostomy, and Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia). However several billed diagnosis and procedure lines lack documentation support and must be removed or have POA/severity corrected. Support for I61.9 as principal (keep, POA=Y, MCC): H&P documents the presenting event and imaging: Emergent CT head demonstrated a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275). The ICH policy requires neuroimaging confirmation of intraparenchymal blood (non-contrast CT) to validate I61 codes: - Non-contrast CT of the brain demonstrating hyperdense (acute) intraparenchymal blood collection within the brain tissue, with the radiologist's report specifying anatomic location (e.g., right basal ganglia, left thalamus, right cerebellar hemisphere) (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Non-Traumatic-Intracerebral-Hemorrhage.docx-b31). These two passages together meet the policy's Validation Criteria for nontraumatic ICH and support I61.9 as the principal diagnosis. Support for obstructive hydrocephalus (keep, change severity to MCC): The H&P and neurosurgery consult document obstructive hydrocephalus with ventricular blood and recommend emergent CSF diversion: the chart documents emergent EVD placement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: 3 | Emergency external ventricular drain placement) and neurosurgery recommended emergent EVD placement with drain settings (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n12, p.45: Recommendations Emergent EVD placement in the right Kocher's point; drain to 15 cmH2O above the tragus; ICP monitoring; osmotherapy; strict SBP control; follow-up CT in 6 hours). The obstructive-hydrocephalus policy designates G91.1 as MCC when imaging/provider documentation confirms obstruction (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Obstructive-Hydrocephalus.docx-b8). Therefore G91.1 is supported and should carry MCC severity (policy source: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Obstructive-Hydrocephalus.docx-b8). Support for acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (keep, POA=Y, MCC): Critical Care documentation demonstrates objective hypoxemia and mechanical ventilation: ABG (02:00): pH 7.32 / PaCO2 47 / PaO2 67 / HCO3 20; P/F 70 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n11, p.721). The acute-respiratory-failure policy allows presumption of objective hypoxemia when the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37). The H&P and progress notes document emergent intubation for airway protection on presentation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: Rapid-sequence intubation was performed for airway protection) and an active problem of prolonged mechanical ventilation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: 5 | Acute respiratory failure with prolonged mechanical ventilation). These meet the policy criteria for J96.01. Support for ventilator-associated Klebsiella pneumonia (J15.9 and B96.1, POA=N): Medication Administration records show treatment with cefepime specifically for Klebsiella VAP (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.694: Cefepime | 2 g | IV q8h | 08/01-08/08 | Klebsiella VAP) and the discharge summary documents a hospital-acquired Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1262, p.1052: hospital-acquired Klebsiella pneumoniae ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime). POA=N for VAP is correct. Procedures supported (kept): EVD insertion and VP shunt are documented. VP shunt operative note documents right frontal ventriculostomy to peritoneum and distal catheter placement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n122, p.43: Under general anesthesia, right frontal ventricular catheter placed. Programmable valve tunneled subcutaneously to peritoneal cavity via mini-laparotomy.). Arterial-line placement is documented (Procedure Note - Arterial Line - Right Radial supports arterial monitoring; conflict checking favors the right radial arterial line procedure note; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n18, p.97: Indication for Procedure: Tight blood pressure monitoring for SBP < 140). Tracheostomy and PEG placement are documented throughout the chart and discharge (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.127 and NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1262, p.1052). Ventilation >96 hours is supported by the active problem list and the prolonged course requiring tracheostomy (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: 5 | Acute respiratory failure with prolonged mechanical ventilation). ETT insertion is supported by the ED/H&P and progress notes (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: Rapid-sequence intubation was performed for airway protection). Unsupported / removed diagnoses and rationale: - I97.5 (Nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage) - removed. Imaging/interpretation and neurology/neurosurgery documentation consistently describe a left basal-ganglia intraparenchymal (hypertensive) hemorrhage with intraventricular extension; the MRI/radiology and consult notes do not document a subdural hematoma (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n42, p.276: Large left basal-ganglia hematoma with expected evolution pattern. No underlying vascular malformation identified. IVH resolving.). The ICH policy explicitly distinguishes intraparenchymal ICH from extraparenchymal subdural hemorrhage (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Non-Traumatic-Intracerebral-Hemorrhage.docx-b11). There is no radiology/provider documentation supporting a subdural diagnosis, so I97.5 should be removed. - A39.0 (Meningococcal meningitis) - removed. No clinical, laboratory, imaging, or infectious-disease documentation of meningitis or meningococcal infection was found; the infectious complication documented and treated was Klebsiella VAP (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.694; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1262, p.1052). Without supporting documentation, A39.0 is not supported. - E22.2 (SIADH) - removed. The chart documents cerebral salt wasting with targeted therapy (fludrocortisone) rather than SIADH: Fludrocortisone | 0.1 mg | PO/PEG BID | 08/08-08/13 | Cerebral salt wasting (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.127). The documentation supports cerebral salt wasting (a different entity) and does not support SIADH coding. - Z98.62 (Presence of intracranial neurostimulator) - removed. The record documents a VP shunt and EVD but no intracranial neurostimulator device; discharge/transfer and procedure notes list VP shunt and tracheostomy/PEG without mention of a neurostimulator or its implantation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1258, p.168: Your brain shunt (VP shunt) drains fluid from your brain to your abdomen; watch for signs of shunt malfunction...). Absent documentation specific to a neurostimulator, Z98.62 is unsupported. POA / severity corrections: - G91.1 (Obstructive hydrocephalus): billed as CC but policy designates obstructive hydrocephalus as MCC when criteria are met (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Obstructive-Hydrocephalus.docx-b8). The documentation meets obstructive-hydrocephalus criteria (ventricular blood and EVD/VP shunt management), so set severity to MCC. - G81.94 (Hemiplegia, right dominant) and R47.1 (dysarthria): both are clearly present on presentation (H&P documents dense right hemiplegia and inability to speak on arrival). POA should be Y (present on admission) rather than N as billed (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: dense right hemiplegia; "... he couldn't move his right side or speak." and the admission neuro exam). Update POA accordingly. - Z99.11 (Dependence on respirator status): documentation shows emergent intubation on presentation and prolonged ventilator dependence with subsequent tracheostomy; POA should be Y (present at/very near admission) rather than billed N (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: Rapid-sequence intubation was performed for airway protection; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1262, p.1052: tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status). Procedures removed for lack of specific documentation in the retrieved chart: - 02HV33Z (Insertion of infusion device into superior vena cava, percutaneous approach) - removed. The record documents multiple central infusions and lines were used, but there is no specific procedural note or operative report found in the retrieved chart that documents insertion of an infusion device into the SVC (the discharge/procedure summaries list EVD, VP shunt, tracheostomy, PEG, arterial line but not a tunneled/implanted infusion device into the SVC) (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1262, p.1052). Keep all other billed procedures that have specific procedure or problem-list documentation (ETT insertion, EVD, VP shunt, arterial line, tracheostomy, PEG, prolonged ventilation assistance >96 hrs). Citations (selected, by document and page): - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: Emergent CT head demonstrated a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus. - RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Non-Traumatic-Intracerebral-Hemorrhage.docx-b31: - Non-contrast CT of the brain demonstrating hyperdense (acute) intraparenchymal blood collection within the brain tissue, with the radiologist's report specifying anatomic location (e.g., right basal ganglia, left thalamus, right cerebellar hemisphere) - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n12, p.45: Recommendations Emergent EVD placement in the right Kocher's point; drain to 15 cmH2O above the tragus; ICP monitoring; osmotherapy; strict SBP control; follow-up CT in 6 hours. - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n122, p.43: Under general anesthesia, right frontal ventricular catheter placed. Programmable valve tunneled subcutaneously to peritoneal cavity via mini-laparotomy. - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n11, p.721: ABG (02:00): pH 7.32 / PaCO2 47 / PaO2 67 / HCO3 20; P/F 70. - RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37: [1] Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is not documented. Emergent intubation may preclude room-air measurement; provider documentation of the clinical urgency is sufficient. - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.694: Cefepime | 2 g | IV q8h | 08/01-08/08 | Klebsiella VAP - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n42, p.276: Large left basal-ganglia hematoma with expected evolution pattern. No underlying vascular malformation identified. IVH resolving. - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1251, p.127: Fludrocortisone | 0.1 mg | PO/PEG BID | 08/08-08/13 | Cerebral salt wasting - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: 3 | Emergency external ventricular drain placement - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n9, p.275: 5 | Acute respiratory failure with prolonged mechanical ventilation - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n18, p.97: Indication for Procedure: Tight blood pressure monitoring for SBP < 140 - NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_19.pdf-n1258, p.168: Your brain shunt (VP shunt) drains fluid from your brain to your abdomen; watch for signs of shunt malfunction (headache, vomiting, worsening confusion). Because multiple billed diagnosis lines lack supporting documentation (I97.5, A39.0, E22.2, Z98.62) and one procedure (02HV33Z) lacks a supporting procedure note, this review results in a Finding and the claim-level diagnosis and procedure lists are corrected below.
rationale_letter: To: Medical Records / Coding Department Re: Audit of Inpatient Claim MR_19 - Determination and Required Coding Corrections We performed a DRG-focused audit of the entire inpatient encounter for patient MR_19. We compared the billed diagnosis and procedure list against the medical record and the applicable coding validation policies. Below is our determination and the corrective action required. Finding: The medical record supports the principal diagnosis of nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus, together with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation and a ventilator-associated Klebsiella pneumonia. However, several billed diagnosis and one billed procedure lack clinical documentation meeting policy validation criteria and must be removed from the coded claim. Basis (examples of supporting documentation relied on): - The admission H&P documents emergent CT demonstrating a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus (Clinical note: Priya Ranganathan, MD; 07/23/2026) - this satisfies the ICH imaging/provider documentation requirement for an I61.- code. - Neurosurgery documented emergent EVD placement for obstructive hydrocephalus and later performed a ventriculoperitoneal shunt when hydrocephalus persisted (operative note 08/09/2026). These procedures meet the surgical validation pathway for ICH and hydrocephalus coding. - Critical care ABG documented PaO2 67 mm Hg and a P/F ratio of 70, and the chart documents emergent intubation and prolonged mechanical ventilation with subsequent tracheostomy; these facts satisfy the acute hypoxemic respiratory failure criteria for J96.01 (policy presumption for objective hypoxemia with provider-documented invasive ventilation). - The chart documents Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime during the admission (medication administration and discharge summary). Corrections required (summary): - Remove diagnoses not supported by the medical record: I97.5 (nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage), A39.0 (meningococcal meningitis), E22.2 (SIADH), and Z98.62 (intracranial neurostimulator) - these conditions are not documented in the radiology/operative/consultation notes or are contradicted by documented alternative diagnoses (e.g., cerebral salt wasting documented and treated rather than SIADH; intraparenchymal basal ganglia hemorrhage documented rather than subdural hematoma). - Correct severity/POA where chart evidence requires it: G91.1 obstructive hydrocephalus meets MCC criteria per policy and documentation (change severity to MCC); G81.94 (hemiplegia, right) and R47.1 (dysarthria) are documented on presentation and should be POA=Y; Z99.11 (dependence on respirator) is present at/near admission and should be POA=Y. - Remove procedure 02HV33Z (insertion of infusion device into SVC) - no procedural note or operative report in the record documents this specific procedure, whereas EVD, VP shunt, arterial line, tracheostomy, PEG, and prolonged ventilation ARE documented. Corrected coding outcome: the claim should retain I61.9 as principal diagnosis and keep the supported high-severity comorbidities and procedures (see the attached revised diagnosis and procedure lists). Please update the coded claim accordingly and re-submit. If you disagree with removal of any code above, please provide the specific source documentation that supports the removed code (operative note, radiology report, or treating-provider note with date/time) so we can reconsider. Absent such documentation, the removals above stand. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
